title: Strengthening of Cooperative Institutions in Vellore
body_text:
To examine the functioning of cooperative institutions across the country, including those in Vellore district of Tamil Nadu, the Ministry of Cooperation (MoC) has adopted a multi-layered institutional mechanism for monitoring cooperative sector initiatives at the State and district levels, with a view to ensuring effective coordination, implementation and monitoring. For this purpose, committees have been constituted at various levels, from the national level to the district level. These include:
i. Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) – Chaired by the Hon’ble Minister of Home Affairs & Cooperation;
ii. National Level Coordination Committee (NLCC) – Chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation;
iii. State Cooperative Development Committee (SCDC) – Chaired by the Chief Secretary of the respective State/UT; and
iv. District Cooperative Development Committee (DCDC) – Chaired by the District Collector of the respective district.
As per information received from the State of Tamil Nadu, two SCDC meetings and two DCDC meetings have been convened so far.
Further, Ministry has launched the ‘Cooperative Ranking Framework’ which provides standardized parameters—including audit compliance, financial performance, and operational activities—that enable the State Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) to conduct independent assessments and take necessary steps to strengthen societies at the State, district, and block levels.
The sector-wise details of the total number and the number of functional cooperative societies in Vellore district are attached at Annexure-A.
The Government has undertaken a series of digital, financial and capacity-building measures to strengthen governance, professional management, service delivery, operational efficiency and outreach of cooperative institutions, including those functioning in Vellore district:
Under the National Plan for formation of new Multipurpose PACS, Dairy and Fishery Cooperative Societies to achieve cooperative coverage in every uncovered Panchayat/village over a period of five years, as on 15.07.2026, a 27 PACS, 940 DCS and 36 FCS have been registered in the State of Tamil Nadu including 11 DCS in the Vellore district. Under the Central Sector Project for Computerization of PACS, 4,561 PACS have been sanctioned and Rs 55.73 Cr have been disbursed to the State of Tamil Nadu. As on 15.07.2026, hardware has been delivered to 4,532 PACS and 4,481 PACS have been onboarded onto the common ERP-based national software including 64 PACS in Vellore District. The initiative is aimed at improving transparency, accounting, audit, monitoring, digital service delivery and integration with the cooperative banking structure. The Model Bye-laws circulated by the Ministry of Cooperation and adopted by the State enable PACS to undertake more than 25 diversified business activities. As per information provided by the State of Tamil Nadu, in Vellore district, 55 PACS are functioning as Common Service Centres and Fair Price Shops; 43 PACS are providing micro-ATM facilities, 55 PACS are working as PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras. Further, 28 PACS are providing agricultural machinery services, 9 are operating Pharmacy/Medical Store, one is operating a Cooperative Medical Shop, 43 PACS have godowns. For improving professional management and long-term institutional sustainability, capacity-building programmes are conducted through the National Council for Cooperative Training. In Tamil Nadu, such programmes are implemented through the Natesan Institute of Cooperative Management, Chennai, and the Institute of Cooperative Management, Madurai. During the last five years, these institutions have trained 1,31,499 participants in the State, including 2,688 participants from Vellore district, in areas such as cooperative governance, financial management, digital literacy, computerization and business diversification. In addition, 4,097 PACS Secretaries in Tamil Nadu have been trained in the effective use of Common Service Centre services; 4 programmes conducted for capacity building of 105 BoDs / Secretaries of M-PACS with emphasis on good governance, professional management, business diversification and effective functioning of societies. Village-level awareness programmes are being conducted to disseminate information regarding Government schemes, institutional credit, market linkages and business diversification. In Tamil Nadu, 560 such programmes have benefited 72,885 members, including 2,234 members from Vellore district. NABARD has conducted various cooperative training programmes covering key areas such as women empowerment for PACS staff, preparation of Business Development Plans, the impact of NPAs on the financial health of PACS, and corporate governance in PACS. During FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26, a total of 578 such cooperative training programmes were conducted in Tamil Nadu, including Vellore, training 15,635 officials. Financial and technical assistance is also available through the National Cooperative Development Corporation for eligible cooperative projects in agriculture, dairy, fisheries, handloom, marketing, processing, storage and allied sectors, subject to prescribed eligibility conditions and project appraisal. The details of financial assistance in the State of Tamil Nadu during last five years by NCDC is provided at Annexure-B

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah detailed the Ministry of Cooperation's multi-layered monitoring mechanism (IMC, NLCC, SCDC, DCDC) for cooperative institutions, with specific data on Vellore district, Tamil Nadu. It highlighted the Cooperative Ranking Framework, PACS computerization progress, formation of new multipurpose PACS/dairy/fishery cooperatives, diversification of PACS business activities, and capacity-building training conducted via NCCT, NABARD and NCDC financial assistance figures for Tamil Nadu.
enrichment.context:
The Ministry of Cooperation, created as a separate ministry in 2021, has been pursuing the vision of 'Sahakar se Samriddhi' (prosperity through cooperation) by strengthening Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) as multi-service rural institutions. Key initiatives include computerization of PACS to integrate them with the cooperative banking structure and improve transparency, the National Plan to set up new multipurpose PACS/Dairy/Fishery cooperatives in every uncovered panchayat, and Model Bye-laws enabling PACS to diversify into over 25 activities like Common Service Centres, Fair Price Shops, godowns, and PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras—aimed at making PACS economically viable beyond just credit disbursal. This reflects a broader push to revive the cooperative sector, which has historically suffered from poor governance, financial mismanagement, and underutilization, especially in states outside the traditional cooperative strongholds like Maharashtra and Gujarat.

Institutions like NABARD (apex agricultural refinance body), NCDC (National Cooperative Development Corporation, providing project financing), and NCCT (National Council for Cooperative Training, delivering capacity-building through institutes like Chennai's Natesan Institute) form the ecosystem supporting this cooperative revival. The district-specific data on Vellore illustrates how national schemes are implemented and monitored at the grassroots, with the multi-tier committee structure (national to district) designed for accountability and coordinated execution—relevant to India's cooperative federalism and Panchayati Raj-linked rural development architecture.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional monitoring mechanism for cooperatives set up by the Ministry of Cooperation:
1. The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) is chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation.
2. The District Cooperative Development Committee (DCDC) is chaired by the District Collector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) is chaired by the Union Home Minister & Minister of Cooperation, not the Secretary (who chairs the National Level Coordination Committee, NLCC). The DCDC is correctly chaired by the District Collector.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Central Sector Project for Computerization of PACS' primarily aims to achieve which of the following?
options: Direct cash transfer of subsidies to farmers
Integration of PACS with the cooperative banking structure through a common ERP-based national software
Setting up of new Regional Rural Banks
Privatization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the computerization initiative aims to improve transparency, accounting, audit, monitoring, digital service delivery, and integration of PACS with the cooperative banking structure via a common ERP-based national software.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) diversification in strengthening rural cooperative institutions in India. Evaluate the role of computerization and capacity-building initiatives in this process.
